newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/mark closes at two-month high in US. [corrected 22:42 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark closes at two-month high in US. [corrected 22:42 gmt]

text.p: (Corrects headline to "two-month high" from "two-week high").

The dollar closed at a two-month high against the mark after the German currency came under attack in Europe and Germany's central bank President Hans Tietmeyer said major nations supported a higher dollar.
Dollar/yen gains were capped by heavy offers above 109.30.
The dollar was carried up to of 1.5010 marks, its highest level since July 16, as the mark fell against the French franc and Italian lira.
The lira surged during speculation on the terms of Italy's possible reentry into Europe's exchange rate mechanism.

"(The lira) has been helped by the debate in Europe over the central parity rate for the lira, when the Italian government decides to rejoin, which should be pretty soon," said David Gilmore, partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics.
The dollar closed at 1.4990/00 marks, up from 1.4903/08 at the open and 109.20/30 yen, up from 108.95/05.
Dollar/mark's gains on Monday were fanned by remarks by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, who said the Group of 10 -- or G10 -- nations agreed on a desire for a strong dollar.
"We all agreed further dollar developement is important and a strong dollar is in the interest of all," Tietmeyer told reporters after a meeting of G10 central bankers in Basle.
The Italian currency was forced out of the European Monetary System in September 1992 amid overwhelming speculation the lira would weaken against other currencies in Europe, particularly the mark.

Mark/lira fell under 1008 on Monday, from about 1015 lira earier in the day. The French and Germans seem to be stepping up pressure for a stronger lira central rate, probably 1000 against the mark, Gilmore said.
The dollar's rise reportedly triggered stop-loss buy orders near 1.4955 and again above the top of the eight-week trading range at 1.4965 marks.
But dealers said offers above 1.5020 marks were heavy.
yet, the market may start to bet on further gains above 1.50 marks, fueling more of a scramble to buy, dealers said.

"After the comments by Tietmeyer, it kind of paves the way a little bit," said Brian Arabia, assistant vice president at ABN-AMRO Bank in Chicago. "If the dollar goes up, it may have room to go further."

Meanwhile, the French franc rebuffed recent gains by the mark after traders tired of speculating that the September 18 release of France's 1997 budget would erode confidence in its ability to meet budget deficit targets for European currency convergence in 1999.
Dealers unwound bets on a weakening franc by selling the mark, which fell below 3.41 French on Monday.
Last week, the Bank of France reportedly intervened several times to defend the falling franc as the mark encroached on the psychologically important 3.43 French level.
This rate was the bottom of the franc's old fluctuation band, before the ERM realignment in August 1993 widened tolerances from plus or minus 2.25 percent to 15 percent.
In other trade, the dollar rose to 1.2222/32 Swiss francs from 1.2147/57 at the open and it fell to Canadian $1.3699/04 from C$1.3725/30.
The pound fell to $1.5567/77 from $1.5608/15 at the open.
The Australian dollar fell to $0.7993/98 from $0.8007/12 at the open.
-- Alden Bentley 212 859 1667
